extracted.intended_audience: theatregoers, critics, aspiring actors and writers — literate 18th-century public (general readers interested in manners, theatre, and writing)
extracted.subtask_description: Normative guidance on judging actors, playwrights, critics, and news-writers: how critics and audiences should behave toward new performers and writers, what faults are forgivable or condemnable, and warnings about the practices of news-writers and superficial authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critic's primary duty
rubrics_metrics.description: The care of the critick should be to distinguish errour from inability, faults of inexperience from defects of nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics should discern what can be corrected by instruction or experience (errors, inexperience) versus what springs from an actor's or writer's natural incapacity. This implies gentle, corrective criticism for improvable faults and sterner measures only for innate defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forbearance toward new performers
rubrics_metrics.description: In every new performer something must be pardoned; Variation of gesture, and flexion of voice, are to be obtained only by experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audiences and critics should tolerate the initial awkwardness of novices (gesture, voice modulation, timidity) because these are acquired by practice. Early imperfections should be overlooked to allow development; excessive severity is unwarranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: When an actor must be expelled
rubrics_metrics.description: If in an actor there appears an utter vacancy of meaning, a frigid equality, a stupid languor, a torpid apathy, the greatest kindness that can be shown him is a speedy sentence of expulsion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between corrigible faults and incurable failure of expression or feeling. An actor displaying permanent vacancy of meaning or apathetic performance should be removed for the good of the art and audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish faults of inexperience from defects of nature
rubrics_metrics.description: The care of the critick should be to distinguish errour from inability, faults of inexperience from defects of nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical implications: restrain vehemence and vociferation (which can be trained), correct irregular action and excess with gentleness; reserve condemnation for those whose nature prevents improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging young poets and dramatists
rubrics_metrics.description: The art of the writer, like that of the player, is attained by slow degrees... the art of dramatick disposition, the contexture of the scenes, the opposition of characters, the involution of the plot, the expedients of suspension, and the stratagems of surprise, are to be learned by practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not permanently discourage writers who lack innate genius for certain poetic faculties if they show promise in learnable craft. Assessors should separate poetic genius (inimitable) from dramaturgical skill (acquirable) and allow room for practice-driven improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of reproof — target vice not trivial faults
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproof should not exhaust its power upon petty failings; let it watch diligently against the incursion of vice, and leave foppery and futility to die of themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism should prioritize correcting morally or substantively harmful faults (vice, corruption) rather than expending energy on trivial vanities or affectations that time will often remove on their own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience behaviour toward performers
rubrics_metrics.description: A publick performer is so much in the power of spectators, that all unnecessary severity is restrained by that general law of humanity, which forbids us to be cruel where there is nothing to be feared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spectators ought to show candour and humanity: avoid cruelty (malicious hissing) and also avoid false praise that deceives the public. A balance is required — helpfully support learners, but do not protect or reward clear incapacity or fraud.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid applauding undeserving or hissing in malice
rubrics_metrics.description: He that applauds him who does not deserve praise, is endeavouring to deceive the publick; he that hisses in malice or sport, is an oppressor and a robber.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social responsibility of the audience: applause for the unworthy misleads the public; malicious hissing harms the performer unjustly. Both are anti-patterns; critics and audiences should aim for honest, humane responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between writers who want to be read and those meant to be studied
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the amusements of idleness is reading without the fatigue of close attention, and the world therefore swarms with writers whose wish is not to be studied, but to be read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that some writing aims at fleeting entertainment (readability) rather than lasting intellectual engagement (study). When evaluating or producing work, consider the author's aim: depth and study-worthiness demand different standards than ephemeral readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnosis of 'news-writing' practices (ethical warning)
rubrics_metrics.description: To write news in its perfection requires such a combination of qualities... To these compositions is required neither genius nor knowledge, neither industry nor sprightliness; but contempt of shame and indifference to truth are absolutely necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Johnson's sardonic criterion highlights how news-writing often relies on falsehood and sensationalism (invented battles, atrocity tales) especially in wartime. As a rubric: be wary of credulity, check sources, and treat news that panders to national pride or sensational cruelty with skepticism. The passage functions as an anti-model for ethical journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensationalism as a common device
rubrics_metrics.description: Scarcely any thing awakens attention like a tale of cruelty... the writer of news never fails in the intermission of action to tell how the enemies murdered children and ravished virgins...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and critique the deliberate use of sensational cruelty to captivate readers; as both creator and critic, call out manipulation of moral disgust and demand proportionate, factual reporting rather than manufactured horror.
